runners_data.name: Ellie's de Vega
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with five consecutive third-to-fourth finishes on good ground over 6f, suggesting consistency without a win threat; Ryan Sexton rides and the Noel Wilson yard is out of form (0/5 in 14 days), limiting confidence.|

runners_data.name: Desert Master
runners_data.note: Antony Brittain runner who has placed twice at 5–6f on good ground and is a genuine hold-up type, but with more closers than the track can accommodate he is likely to find himself in midfield rather than his preferred rear position, blunting his finishing kick.|

runners_data.name: Bishop's Glory
runners_data.note: Prominent racer stepping back to a more familiar 6f after a run of 5f starts on slower ground; the Ramsden yard has had a recent winner (1/11 in 14 days) and Tom Kiely-Marshall's 5lb claim is useful in a big-field handicap — his natural front-end position is an asset here.|

runners_data.name: Indy's Angel
runners_data.note: Habitual hold-up performer with a string of mid-to-rear finishes at 6–8f on good ground; true trailing position is unavailable in this field, meaning Aiden Brookes will be riding from further forward than ideal, which the form figures on turf (0W1P from 15 similar-going runs) do little to inspire confidence in.|

runners_data.name: Hyrcanian
runners_data.note: Ron Barr handler whose horse carries a fade-in-finish flag and has finished eighth or worse in the majority of recent efforts; the redistribution to a midfield berth compounds the issue for a horse that needs a truly strong pace to mount any challenge, and that pace is unlikely to materialise.|

runners_data.name: The Floors Munky
runners_data.note: Three-year-old who has finished ninth, eleventh and tenth in recent starts and also carries a fade flag; the 44-day break and switch to a shorter 6f trip after attempts at 7–8f are points of interest, but the redistribution away from a true hold-up berth leaves Alex Jary (3lb claim) with limited options tactically.|

runners_data.name: Petes Diamond
runners_data.note: Joey Ramsden's three-year-old has struggled at 6–7f on good ground in recent starts and is another whose natural position at the rear of the field cannot be secured in this unusually hold-up-heavy field; Andrew Mullen has ridden the horse before but the form string offers little encouragement.|

runners_data.name: Mister Sky Blue
runners_data.note: Connor Beasley takes the ride on this prominent-style 4yo who carries blinkers and has two placings from six runs on good ground at 6f; well suited by the likely controlled pace up front and the flat Thirsk track, he is a natural front-rank traveller in the right scenario.|

runners_data.name: Hurstwood
runners_data.note: PJ McDonald on a 9yo with consistent form figures of 6th–9th at 6f on good ground; Niven's horse is a genuine hold-up type who cannot get his preferred position in this field, and ten previous runs at this trip on similar going without a win tells its own story.|

runners_data.name: Golden Prosperity
runners_data.note: Veteran 7yo who has won twice and placed four times from 15 similar-going runs, suggesting genuine competitiveness, but the Tony Coyle & Kaine Wood runner races as a closer and is another whose rearward spot is compromised by the volume of hold-up types in this field; blinkers noted.|

runners_data.name: Thehunnebelllegacy
runners_data.note: Richard & Fahey yard in strong form (6/69 in 14 days) and this 3yo has shown consistent mid-pack placings at 6f on good and good-to-firm; Warren Fentiman's 3lb claim is a bonus, and if the field splits this horse could outrun its hold-up tag more easily than most.|

runners_data.name: Up The Monk
runners_data.note: Michael Appleby runner returning after a 102-day absence — the longest layoff in the field — wearing a visor; won at 6f on standard ground in the past but that form is distant and the fitness question after over three months off is significant.|

runners_data.name: Everydaysasaturday
runners_data.note: Declan Carroll has had three winners in 14 days, giving some trainer confidence, but this 3yo carries blinkers and has finished fifth to eleventh in five recent starts with no win or place at 6f on good ground; the hold-up style is further squeezed here.|

runners_data.name: Stormy Pearl
runners_data.note: Consistent 6yo who has placed four times from fifteen good-ground runs and scored once, with a very active recent record at this exact trip; David Thompson's runner wears a hood and has genuine form figures that make her competitive if getting any sort of clear run from off the pace.|

runners_data.name: Dolly's Delight
runners_data.note: Ivan Furtado's 4yo has a win and two placings from fourteen similar-going runs and Jason Hart's experience in big-field handicaps is an asset; however her 6–7f form suggests a slightly longer trip suits and the hold-up style is the least effective shape in today's race.|

runners_data.name: Night Emperor
runners_data.note: Joanna Mason partners this 4yo who has placed at 6f on good ground twice in five recent starts; the Tina Jackson yard has just one runner in the 14-day window and the 34-day break since last run creates a minor freshness question, though the form is solid enough at this level.|

runners_data.name: Mrs Trump
runners_data.note: Paul Midgley's 6yo is the confirmed lone front runner in this race and is perfectly placed to dictate terms; two wins from fifteen similar-going runs show she can fire on good-to-firm ground, and the controlled gallop she sets should play to her strengths — the STYLE_FIT flag is a secondary consideration given she is likely to lead by default.|

runners_data.name: Barmyblade
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's 4yo has three wins and four placings from fifteen similar-going runs, making him one of the most proven horses on form in this field; wears blinkers and is a true hold-up type who would ordinarily be dangerous, but David Allan will struggle to find his natural trailing position with so many closers forced into midfield.|

runners_data.name: Uncle Sam
runners_data.note: Tom Eaves partners this 4yo who has placed twice from five runs at 5–6f on standard ground; Ray Craggs has just one runner in the recent window and the horse is a genuine hold-up performer whose rearward berth is unavailable today, making it hard to see how he can reproduce his best despite the talent shown in those two near-misses.|

races.paceDynamic: Mrs Trump is the sole confirmed front runner in this 19-runner 6f handicap on good-to-firm ground at Thirsk, and with no genuine rival to pressure her from the gates she can dictate a controlled, honest gallop rather than a scorching pace. Bishop's Glory and Mister Sky Blue are the only other horses mapped prominently, meaning the early order will be relatively settled and the pace sustainable rather than suicidal. The field contains a heavy concentration of hold-up types — Uncle Sam, Hurstwood, Golden Prosperity, Barmyblade, Desert Master and others are true closers who are unlikely to secure their natural rearward berth and will instead be shuffled into midfield, compromising their effectiveness and muddying the final-furlong picture. With Mrs Trump able to control fractions unchallenged, this race shape firmly favours horses who can race prominently or just off the pace in the first three or four, as the moderate early tempo will not soften the ground for closers to come from off it.

watchPoints.text: Mrs Trump is the sole front runner and if she gets a clean break from the stalls she could lead by daylight within a furlong — watch her early jumping as an uncontested lead on good-to-firm at Thirsk over 6f is a significant tactical advantage in this field.

With at least nine genuine hold-up types compressed into midfield, the draw and early positioning battle in the opening furlong will be chaotic — any horse caught wide or badly blocked at the three-furlong pole is effectively racing out of contention.

Barmyblade and Golden Prosperity both show strong similar-going form figures but are racing structurally out of role today; if either David Allan or Jake Dickson can engineer an early drop to the rear despite the traffic, they carry enough raw ability to make the frame.

Thehunnebelllegacy is trained by the in-form Fahey yard (6/69 in 14 days) and Warren Fentiman's claim brings the weight down — monitor market moves as shrewd stable support in a handicap of this size often signals a horse expected to outperform its mapped position.

The going report confirms good-to-firm at Thirsk all day, and Stormy Pearl has eleven runs on similar ground at this trip with consistent placings — any significant drying of the surface further into the afternoon could subtly benefit horses with the deepest good-to-firm profiles, of which she is among the strongest.

runners_data.name: Celtic Arrow
runners_data.note: Lightly raced 3yo for Julie Camacho returning after 112 days off, with a consistent recent form string of 3-4-2 over the same course and distance configuration; has only run on Standard (AW) ground in recent history so Good to Firm turf is a genuine unknown, but the Camacho yard has a live runner here and Ryan Sexton takes the ride with first-time or early-career ambition.|

runners_data.name: Masai Angel
runners_data.note: Richard & Fahey yard in strong 14-day form (5/61), and this filly ran on Good ground last time (3rd) suggesting the surface is fine; however, her natural racing style means she will be towards the rear of the field, and a steady Showtown-controlled pace is unlikely to set up the late run she needs to get involved from that position.|

runners_data.name: Country Artiste
runners_data.note: Craig Lidster's gelding has a poor recent form string (55-670) and a sim-going record of just 0W2P across 10 visits to Good-type ground; his natural pattern sees him race from the back, and in a race without a hot pace he will struggle to make up ground from the rear of the field on Good to Firm at Thirsk.|

runners_data.name: Hares Bredth
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby has a strong 14-day strike rate (8/104) and this horse won last time out over 6f Good (1/6f/GOO) showing genuine current form; he wears a hood (hg:t) and is a hold-up horse who has demonstrated he can produce a telling finish on Good ground, but the steady pace Showtown will set may mean the race is over before he can land his challenge.|

runners_data.name: Concert
runners_data.note: Tom Marquand rides for Jack Channon and this filly ran third last time over 6f AW; her sim-going record of just 1W2P from nine starts on similar ground is moderate, and as a hold-up horse over 6f at Thirsk without a true pace to run into, this race shape presents a difficult tactical picture for her to overcome.|

runners_data.name: Liverpool Star
runners_data.note: Joanna Mason takes the ride and this filly won last time out over 6f Good (1/6f/GOO) — the most relevant recent form line in the race and carrying a sim-going record of 1W3P from 13 runs; she races off the pace and that winning run shows she can finish powerfully, but she needs a better-than-steady gallop to exploit her finishing kick in a race dominated by Showtown.|

runners_data.name: Simba's Pride
runners_data.note: Michael Dods' colt carries an outstanding Good-ground profile — 2W3P from eight identical-surface starts including two wins at 6f Good — and Mark Winn keeps things simple from a prominent position; this is the horse whose natural style suits this race shape best, close enough to Showtown to pounce without needing a searching pace.|

runners_data.name: King's Road Dandy
runners_data.note: David Nolan rides and the horse has only three career starts (3-5-8) with a win over 6f Good showing some ability; he is a true hold-up horse by style and will race further back than the map shows — in a race without genuine pace to chase, getting competitive from the rear over a flat 6f is a significant ask.|

runners_data.name: Showtown
runners_data.note: Kevin Ryan's colt is the race's sole confirmed front runner and wears a hood (hg:p), but his recent form (5th, 4th in last two) on softer ground tempers confidence he can simply lead and win; his STYLE_FIT flag reflects that he is being asked to fill a role he may not fully relish, and whether he has enough acceleration to hold rivals once the race quickens in the final furlong is the critical question.|

runners_data.name: Saucy Jane
runners_data.note: Jack Morland's yard sends her back 19 days after a run and she wears a hood (hg:p); her sim-going record (1W4P from 14 starts) shows she is regularly competitive on Good-adjacent ground, but she is a hold-up type who needs a strong tempo — with Showtown unlikely to stretch the field, getting involved late over 6f here looks difficult.|

runners_data.name: Go Lockers Go
runners_data.note: Daniel Tudhope, a top-tier sprint jockey, takes the ride for Michael Bell and this horse's form of 1-1-2-2 in the last four represents the strongest recent strike rate in the race; a headgear mark (hg:h) and Good-ground sim form of 1W3P from eight starts makes him dangerous, but as a hold-up horse he remains dependent on enough pace to deliver his finish — Tudhope's tactical awareness is the best-case mitigant.|

runners_data.name: Houndhill
runners_data.note: Nigel Tinkler's gelding wears a visor (hg:v) and has a recent win over 5f AW, but the last Good-ground outing was a 6th of 6f, and his sim-going record of 0W1P from nine similar-ground starts is thin on confidence; he races prominently which suits this shape, but his form trajectory (2-6-8-1-0) is erratic and the visor has to repeatedly do its job.|

races.paceDynamic: Showtown is the one confirmed front runner in this 12-runner 6f handicap on Good to Firm ground at Thirsk, and with no credible pace rival to seriously challenge from the gate, he is likely to bowl along at a sustainable gallop rather than a lung-bursting tempo. The majority of this field — Concert, Liverpool Star, King's Road Dandy, Go Lockers Go, Saucy Jane, Hares Bredth, Masai Angel, and Country Artiste — are genuine hold-up or off-the-pace types, meaning the early sections will be relatively controlled and the race is unlikely to be run at a frenetic pace that would naturally set up those closers. Simba's Pride and Houndhill provide prominent coverage just behind Showtown, so the leading group will be small and compact through the first half of the race before the pack gathers. This race shape — a lone, uncontested front runner setting a measured tempo — strongly favours prominent and near-prominent horses who can travel in the slipstream and pounce in the final furlong, rather than true deep closers who need a fast pace to drag them into contention. Several horses tagged as redistributed (King's Road Dandy, Masai Angel, Country Artiste, and Hares Bredth) are genuine hold-up horses placed in midfield on the map because too many closers crowd the rear; the horses most likely to actually secure a useful position close to the pace are Simba's Pride, Houndhill, and Celtic Arrow.

watchPoints.text: Simba's Pride — watch whether Mark Winn secures a position directly behind Showtown in the first two furlongs; if he does, this horse's 2W3P Good-ground sprint record makes him the most dangerous horse to the leader at the top of the straight.

Go Lockers Go — Daniel Tudhope's positioning in the first half is critical; if he gets a clean run from midfield around the 2f pole he could arrive late with a big finish, but any traffic from the congested pack of hold-up horses will cost him his chance.

Showtown — monitor the early strides to see whether Simba's Pride or Houndhill apply any pressure to his lead; if he gets a completely uncontested rail bowl, his chance of lasting home improves significantly over the scenario where he is niggled at early.

Hares Bredth — Tim Easterby's yard is in strong recent form (8/104 over 14 days) and the horse won last time on Good ground; despite the unfavourable race shape for hold-up horses, if the pace unexpectedly quickens this one is capable of finishing through the field rapidly.

Liverpool Star — the only other horse in the field with a recent 6f Good win, and Joanna Mason knows this horse well; worth tracking in the final quarter-mile to see whether a strong pace develops that pulls her into contention.

races.name: Weatherbys Global Stallions App Handicap

runners_data.name: Westmorian
runners_data.note: Consistent 6f performer for Grant Tuer but has finished 7th, 8th and 9th in recent starts on Good ground; a naturally prominent racer who is likely to find himself further back than ideal given the crowded pace positions, which tempers confidence significantly.

runners_data.name: Bergerac
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old with cheekpieces, trained by Kevin Ryan, who has had a rough time of late with a string of poor finishes — his best recent effort was a 4th three runs back, and he typically races from hold-up to be delivered late; nothing here strongly suggests a reversal of fortunes.

runners_data.name: Juan Les Pins
runners_data.note: Michael Appleby's consistent 9-year-old has a remarkable recent record showing 1-2-1-2-3 form, winning and placing repeatedly on Good ground at 5-6f; nonetheless he is a horse who wants to race prominently and is likely to be shuffled back by the congestion, which is the key risk against his otherwise strong profile.

runners_data.name: Mister Sox
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's 6-year-old is very lightly weighted and runs just 10 days after his last outing, with solid placed form on Good ground at 6f; he genuinely wants to be up with the pace but the crowded prominent berths mean he may have to settle for a midfield position against his natural inclination.

runners_data.name: Deep Havana
runners_data.note: NON-RUNNER — was the confirmed front-runner in the original race map; his absence removes the one horse guaranteed to lead and fundamentally alters the pace shape of this race.

runners_data.name: Strong Warrior
runners_data.note: Warren Fentiman claims 3lb on this Fahey-trained 4-year-old, who has two career wins on Good going and was placed 3rd last time out; a genuine hold-up horse who needs the pace to collapse in front of him, and his best form on Good ground makes him one to watch if the race is falsely run.

runners_data.name: Indian Run
runners_data.note: Julie Camacho's 5-year-old has placed twice at 6f on Good ground recently including a 2nd last time, and is a true hold-up type who will be ridden for a late run; consistent course profile, though he needs things to go right in front to reach the leaders.

runners_data.name: Lord Roxby
runners_data.note: Nigel Tinkler's 4-year-old has won twice over 6f on Good ground and was placed 4th most recently; with Deep Havana now a non-runner, Lord Roxby becomes the most likely de facto leader and is positioned to benefit most from dictating a controlled pace.

runners_data.name: American Style
runners_data.note: Kevin Ryan's 4-year-old has struggled recently with three finishing positions of 9th, 3rd and 0, and while he possesses decent earlier form including two wins on Good, he is a natural prominent racer likely displaced to midfield by the crowded pace scenario, reducing his chances materially.

runners_data.name: Veblen Good
runners_data.note: Daniel Tudhope takes the ride on David O'Meara's 4-year-old, who won at Thirsk on Good ground last time out over this exact trip; a prominent type who should be able to secure a good position just behind any leader and his course-winning form on identical going makes him a strong profile fit.

runners_data.name: Novello Lad
runners_data.note: Paul Midgley's 5-year-old has won back-to-back recently, both on Good and Soft ground, and David Nolan's experience is a significant plus; he sits prominently and his 13-from-15 strike rate on similar going combined with three wins and nine places in that sample marks him as the standout form horse for this race shape.

races.paceDynamic: Deep Havana (now a NON-RUNNER) was the one confirmed front-runner listed, meaning this 6f field at Thirsk loses its only genuine pace-setter, and the race now lacks a horse willing to commit fully from the off. With Deep Havana absent, Lord Roxby becomes the most logical early leader from the prominent types, but he faces no pressure from a single dominant pace-setter — instead, a cluttered midfield of Westmorian, Juan Les Pins, Mister Sox and American Style, all natural prominent racers who cannot all secure their preferred position, will jostle for space and create a moderate-to-muddled early tempo rather than a true end-to-end test. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than the race shape can accommodate: Lord Roxby is best placed to actually secure the lead, with Veblen Good and Novello Lad poised just behind, while Westmorian, Juan Les Pins, Mister Sox and American Style are all likely to find themselves racing further back than ideal. On Good to Firm ground at a flat, straight 6f, a steadily-run or falsely-paced race strongly favours horses with tactical versatility who can be placed just off a modest pace and quicken late — the profile that benefits most is a handy prominent type with a sharp recent turn of foot, particularly those whose form already shows winning on identical going.

scenarios.body: If the surplus of prominent types causes early crowding, interfering with several runners' rhythm and producing a rough, uneven race shape.

watchPoints.text: Lord Roxby's ability to secure the lead uncontested is critical — if any of the displaced prominent types (Westmorian, Mister Sox, Juan Les Pins) push forward aggressively, his race plan is disrupted and the whole race shape changes.

Novello Lad's back-to-back winning momentum and Tudhope's booking on Veblen Good (course winner, same trip, identical going) create a direct clash between the two most prominent profile fits — watch their positions at the 2f pole.

Strong Warrior and Indian Run are genuine hold-up types who need a true pace to be set — with no confirmed front-runner after Deep Havana's non-runner, the slow-gallop risk is high and both could find themselves with no race to run into.

American Style and Westmorian are both natural pace horses racing out of role in a congested prominent group — any early scrimmaging or interference in the first furlong involving these two could compromise multiple runners' chances simultaneously.

Good to Firm conditions confirmed for this 4:10 race on the Thirsk going report — all prominent and prominent-adjacent horses with strong Good-ground form (Novello Lad, Juan Les Pins, Mister Sox) are at no going disadvantage, and the flat straight 6f track at Thirsk offers minimal shelter from pace tactics.

races.name: William Hill Summer Cup Saturday 1st August Book Now Handicap

runners_data.name: Tattie Bogle
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston's hold-up four-year-old arrives on a short 8-day turnaround in strong recent form (three wins and two seconds in last six), handles Good ground well, and this 7f Thirsk trip suits — the main angle is straightforward: gets cover, produces a late run.

runners_data.name: Farandaway
runners_data.note: The sole front-runner here — Grant Tuer's horse has raced almost exclusively over 5-6f at Southwell and steps markedly up in trip on an 81-day break; the lack of pressure gives it every chance to set a comfortable gallop, but stamina beyond 6f is unproven and the style fit at 7f on turf is a question.

runners_data.name: War Howl
runners_data.note: Poor recent form (six consecutive finishes outside the top nine) and the flagged fade in the finish make this a difficult recommendation regardless of scenario; Ben Haslam's runner handles the going but is clearly out of form.

runners_data.name: Al Muqdad
runners_data.note: David O'Meara's six-year-old ran just five days ago, wears a hood, and has placed twice at 7f on Good ground in recent history — Conor Whiteley takes off a useful 5lb, and if the horse gets a prominent position early it is not without each-way claims.

runners_data.name: In A Hurry
runners_data.note: Tudhope takes the ride for stablemate trainer O'Meara and the horse's best recent run was a second on Good ground over 7f — the topspeed figures and going suitability (10/12 in similar conditions) are encouraging, though form has been patchy at 8f and it clearly prefers this shorter trip.

runners_data.name: Avatar Jet
runners_data.note: Declan Carroll's five-year-old is a genuine hold-up horse whose best form has come over 8f at Southwell and who is being asked to drop in trip on turf — the redistribution to midfield reflects congestion at the rear, but its natural inclination is to come from off the pace and the shorter trip here is a concern.

runners_data.name: Vince Le Prince
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's six-year-old has placed twice over this C&D trip in Good ground and is a consistent hold-up performer; headgear (tp) is familiar, but soft-ground form dominates recent runs and the quicker conditions today may blunt its finishing kick slightly.

runners_data.name: Men Of Honour
runners_data.note: Ruth Carr's four-year-old has a poor recent record with five finishes outside the top six in six runs; its natural race from the back will be further compromised in a field packed with hold-up horses, and form at 6f on Good ground has been weak throughout.

runners_data.name: King Of War
runners_data.note: Michael Wigham's seven-year-old ran just yesterday (1-day turnaround is striking), wears tp headgear, and has won three of his last fifteen on similar ground — Alexandra Egan claims 7lb and the horse is a genuine hold-up type whose recent 1st over 7f on Good ground is the standout piece of evidence in this race.

runners_data.name: Way To Dubai
runners_data.note: Michael Appleby's seven-year-old has zero wins or places from 15 runs on similar going, and recent form shows a series of mid-field to rear finishes; even from a hold-up position the form simply does not support strong claims here.

runners_data.name: Singoura
runners_data.note: Gemma Tutty's four-year-old has placed twice at 7f on Good ground and finished second in a comparable race, but the trainer's 14-day record of 0 wins from 10 runners is a concern; Joanna Mason rides and the horse is a hold-up type whose finishing efforts have been consistent without winning.

runners_data.name: We've Got This
runners_data.note: Ivan Furtado's four-year-old runs prominently, which is a genuine advantage in a field where most rivals are hold-up types — Tom Eaves takes the ride and the horse has a placed record at slightly longer trips, though it has not won since a 2nd at 8f on Soft and switching back to Good ground is unknown territory.

runners_data.name: Imperial Guard
runners_data.note: Michael Dods' five-year-old has been running over 5-6f and steps up to 7f here; recent form shows 8th and 8th in last two runs on Good ground and the horse is naturally a hold-up type that has struggled for consistency — the step up in trip is the main unknown.

runners_data.name: Rory's Gold
runners_data.note: Simon Waugh's four-year-old (amateur jockey Amie Waugh, 3lb claim) has zero wins or places on similar going from nine attempts and placed most recently over 8f Soft — the drop in trip and switch to Good ground are both untested, and the trainer's 14-day blank record (0/1) adds no confidence.

races.paceDynamic: Farandaway is the sole confirmed front-runner in a field of 14, and with no genuine challenger for the lead, Grant Tuer's four-year-old should be able to dictate at a controlled, sustainable gallop on Good to Firm ground at Thirsk over seven furlongs. The pace is unlikely to be pressured, meaning splits may be relatively even with the real race beginning in the final two furlongs — conditions that historically favour those who can track the leader and quicken from a prominent position. The majority of the field — including Avatar Jet, Vince Le Prince, Men Of Honour, King Of War, Way To Dubai, Singoura, Imperial Guard, and Rory's Gold — are true hold-up types redistributed into midfield on the map because the field cannot accommodate that many genuine closers at the rear; the horses most likely to actually secure a prominent tracking position are We've Got This and, to a lesser degree, Al Muqdad. This race shape strongly favours hold-up horses with a sharp late kick, provided the early tempo from Farandaway is sufficient to string the field out and leave them with enough pace to aim at in the closing stages — pure front-runners and those needing a strong gallop to close into are the key profiles to watch.

watchPoints.text: Farandaway's stamina for 7f on turf is entirely unproven — watch in the market for any drifting that suggests connections or punters share this concern, as it is the pivotal factor in whether the controlling shape holds.

King Of War raced just yesterday and a 1-day turnaround is highly unusual — watch for any veterinary or jockey change declarations before the off, as fitness and recovery are legitimate race-morning risks.

The redistribution of eight genuine hold-up horses into midfield means the closing straight at Thirsk could become severely congested — watch for traffic issues and crowding in the final two furlongs, especially for Avatar Jet, Vince Le Prince, and Men Of Honour who will all be seeking the same gap.

In A Hurry and Tattie Bogle are running back quickly (9 and 8 days respectively) — watch their pre-race demeanour in the paddock, as horses returning fast from a previous run can show signs of fatigue or freshness that alter their tactical approach.

We've Got This is one of only two genuine prominent types alongside Farandaway — if it tracks the leader comfortably through the early stages, it will be the clearest beneficiary of a controlled tempo and worth monitoring through the early furlongs.
